assumptions: The GTF and the record share a coordinate space: the same genome build, or coordinates_only stated.
limits: Refuses on a build mismatch; intervals that fall off the record are reported, not trimmed.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which features from this GTF land on the open record, and which do not fit?

description: Put the features from a GTF in this project onto the open record. A GTF lists features and their positions and carries no sequence, so this is how one reaches a molecule. It REFUSES unless something says the two are in the same coordinate space: if the file names a genome build and the record names the same one it proceeds; if they name different ones it refuses outright; if either is silent it refuses until you pass coordinates_only, which states that you are applying the intervals as positions in this record's own numbering with no genome correspondence checked. Reports what would not fit rather than trimming it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

coordinates_only.description: state that you are applying the intervals as COORDINATES — positions in this record’s own numbering — with no genome correspondence checked. Applying coordinates on that basis is a claim about your own data, and the run records it as the basis it used. Required whenever either side is silent about its assembly; it cannot rescue two assemblies that disagree.

file.description: the annotation file in this project, by name. Unset with exactly one present uses it; with several, this refuses and names them rather than picking.

sequence.description: the seqid within the file whose features to apply (a GTF names one per row). Unset with exactly one present uses it; with several, this refuses and names them — applying the wrong chromosome's intervals is the mistake this parameter exists to prevent.

name: apply_feature_file

added.description: how many features were written — branch on this rather than counting

basis.description: what earned the apply: 'matched' when both assemblies agreed, 'coordinate-space-only' when you stated it. A run's provenance, not a status

duplicate.description: how many were already on the record at the same span, strand and type, so they were not written twice

outOfRange.description: the features whose spans run past the end of the record, each with the end it really has. Reported, never trimmed: a span cut to fit is a different feature

record.description: the open record with the applied features added
